title: Find rank-compatible BIT grade exchanges and prove their address-mixing limits
body:
## Result

A finite exact census identifies three triples and 32 quadruples that can meet the full-field rank test at every integer width and cover the original 36-call BIT deficit at 0.00388 under neutral unrestricted mixing. It covers equal grade sums and counts, old grades 1–6 and new grades 1–8, and exactly two to four lanes. The `(1,5,6)→(2,2,8)` and `(1,4,4,5)→(2,2,3,7)` toy constructions reproduce every forward and adjoint basis column with address-dependent linear extraction.

Two algebraic invariants delimit the route. The unordered-axis-pair representation rules out all 35 profiles with any mixture of common-axis permutations, including noncommuting ones. A determinant-sign specialization rules out two triples and 16 quadruples even with finite rational-linear address maps. The strongest remaining grade-seven quadruple would cross on 14 uses and has formal full-36 BIT margin +0.04842360493697922. It needs a legal non-coordinate binding or address-dependent extraction, plus its actual cost. The rational 48-call component is unchanged at +0.13897452233425271. No portable physical caller or new κ bound is asserted.

## Native geometry witness

The actual grade-two MOVE `0→113` at clock 2212 (field 1307) and grade-three MOVE `62→313` at clock 1238 (field 1028) cannot share a coordinate permutation basis. Their two-chunk rational interchange product has traces 10, 8, 10, and 16 through the fourth power. A permutation satisfies tr(A²) ≥ tr(A), because squaring fixes two-cycles as well as fixed coordinates. The exact difference here is −2, also after adding the fixed spectators. This shows the native atlas has a concrete feature outside the common-axis obstruction. Physically composing the complete four-lane exchange remains open.

## Replay

Native #7786 `89a67c404226d51028e135de2b9169e9020d57af` and exact signed #7830 profiles `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Archive SHA-256 `d5f130265cbb896a0111e70ade11fc907d3869438e2c28a9df18e383f50ce061`. Fresh manifests and `python3 -I -B verify_profiles.py` passed the exact price and width census, both forward/adjoint abstract controls and a corrupted mapper check. A separate `python3 -I -B geometry_bridge.py` replay rebuilt both nested projectors and the exact rational product traces. The earlier archive remains available on the initial head `86f59c151f63131d30617eac6b980fe80ea21924`.

## Prior work and open next questions

The cross-LOCAL proof handles a neutral two-to-one lane merger. The fixed-chart tests in #8022 preserve the old paid itinerary. This route keeps the paid count while changing grades, so a later constructive test must specify which non-coordinate adapters or typed extraction become physically available before granting a saving.

Canonical main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`. The comparable complete bound comes from #7863 `b3e4412fe01f07dc58305616fabf96345f49a781` and replay #7973 `ac3df5d5c8889f464f575e32dfea43714abf08ca`. Clear1nsight prepared this proof with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds and the native, caller, and verifier contributors retained in the archive.
